title: AI Companies Use Internal Models to Break Cryptographic Protocols
summary:
The newest models developed by leading artificial intelligence labs are being deployed in private attempts to crack the foundations of modern encryption. Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson reported that some companies have quietly begun using their non-public models to probe whether they can break important cryptographic protocols and primitives, according to sources.

Aaronson noted that among the 722 mathematical results recently published by OpenAI, there is a striking lack of breakthroughs in cryptography, adding that the US government has censored academic results on quantum cryptanalysis. Rumors also suggest that OpenAI's most recent release of mathematical findings is the first of three planned batches.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
He also adds this, to which I agree:

'Also noteworthy is the striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the 722 mathematical results OpenAI published. I've witnessed first-hand the US government censoring academic quantum cryptanalysis results. Backroom interventionism is my base case.'

Things are probably further along than it seems. This is true in many areas right now. There are also persistent rumors that the OpenAI math release yesterday was only the first batch of three.
